additional_info.subject: RE: ID0479450-DC/Si-D/IT-[MP/R9 170002644] Type 2 Cable Fused CRM:03042000497
additional_info.body:
Ciao Valerio,
I am coming back to you regarding this case on AC plug melted. Following our previous conversation, today I had some time to check the logs:
As I anticipated you, when it comes to AC charging, we do not get much information from the logs, as the SECC is not logging for AC, and we do not have temperature sensors on the socket.
I checked the logs on 19.02.2026, and we have #2 charging sessions. I believe the 2 sessions are done by two different clients, as the IdTags in the RemoteStartTransaction are different, but I cannot exclude that.
The first session was also a short session (around 1.30 mins), before the charger received the RemoteStopTransaction.
Same goes for the last session. In the logs, that you find attached, I could not see anything weird or suspicious. After the session was stopped, the charger was rebooted immediately. I attach the logs to this email for your convenience.
Based on this, here what should be the way forward:
From an operational point of view, the colleagues form second level already suggested you which components to replace.
As we discussed, please conduct a further onsite inspection and verify if other components on the AC line (not only the socket) are damaged and need to be replaced.
From a safety and quality point of view, I will proceed in these days to open an
8D report.
According to our process, that's the way to report and have Quality department investigate on such cases. They will get in touch with you if required.
Based on this, the ticket should stay in your queue for the repair, and I will get back to you once the 8D report has been created.
With kind regards,
Fosco Servidei
Siemens AG
eMobility Customer Service
